title: What Living Buildings 2.0 Is
definition: Living Buildings 2.0: next-gen buildings that are alive.
description:
Living Buildings 2.0: next-gen buildings that are alive. This is Future Architecture & Building at its most ambitious — living walls research, building logistics engineering and organism care operations converging on a single goal: making building hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Architecture & Building will decide metabolism outcomes this century. Living Buildings 2.0 is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working building hulls, the larger living walls vision stalls, and with it, the building logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents Living Buildings 2.0 in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

title: Real Research Today: Living Buildings 2.0
definition: Today's documented research behind Living Buildings 2.0.
description:
The road to Living Buildings 2.0 is already being paved. Robotics in construction (Built Robotics, Dusty Robotics) automates layout and earthworks. 3D-printed buildings (ICON, COBOD) print homes in days with robotic gantries.

NASA's 3D-Printed Habitat Challenge advanced off-world construction methods. Together these programs form the living walls foundation that Living Buildings 2.0 will build on — the building logistics results, the organism care methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as building logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

title: 2030 — First building hulls districts certified: living walls assembly
definition: 2030 milestone on the Living Buildings 2.0 roadmap.
description:
First building hulls districts certified: living walls assembly at half the time and carbon of legacy builds.

What must be true first: the living walls results have to replicate outside the lab, building logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and organism care operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed living walls demonstrations, building logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting organism care uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Living Buildings 2.0
definition: Estimates Living Buildings 2.0 readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Living Buildings 2.0 components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a building hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Living Buildings 2.0 Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Living Buildings 2.0 operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Living Buildings 2.0 installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 71212 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where living walls monitoring, building logistics redundancy, or organism care maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Living Buildings 2.0 Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Living Buildings 2.0: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Living Buildings 2.0 — next-gen buildings that are alive.

Phase 1 — Prove (living walls): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (building logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (organism care): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (metabolism): building hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and architecture-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
